    #62422. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (758 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (758 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars.
    • Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.
    • Typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

    It’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

    Typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

    The other significant win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

    These satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the debut of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the firm was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

    It has been revealed that escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their latest trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

    Recent findings suggest that by the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

    Sources indicate that this is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

    Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and launched themselves into outer space.

    In a recent development, the tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

    “With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a new strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, mentioned in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”.

    The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, released its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

    Industry observers note that despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX debuted, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations. Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other users.

    Also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

    According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse said the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

    These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing people’ private data,” Reuters said.

    Reuters said “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

    Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she stated she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

    Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

    Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

    The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

    Similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

    Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

    These are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

    Industry observers note that as a tech giant, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

    Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

    Sources indicate that public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if people believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

    Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

    Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

    Signal to restrict screenshots over AI agent concerns – again

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set newly introduced limits on screenshots.
    • Whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers.
    • Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set newly introduced limits on screenshots. The company will prevent screenshotting in its iOS 27 app and “when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android,” Signal President Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post Friday.

    Whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers. These features observe what’s on a user’s screen as context for completing requests.

    Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.

    It has been revealed that “Your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” Whittaker noted. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

    Signal also blocked screenshots last year in response to Microsoft’s controversial Recall AI feature, which could capture screenshots of Signal chats on devices running Windows 11.

    Signal’s move is another reminder of how Significant Tech’s AI strategy trickles downstream. As AI features have moved from services external to the OS (like chatbots from OpenAI or Anthropic) to further inside of it, third-party apps have to adapt to conditions that undermine their hard-won privacy infrastructure.

    Also: How I use Meta Muse safely to stretch my AI budget – and what I never let it do.

    Industry observers note that just last week, researchers at Google DeepMind used AI agents to formally verify Signal’s code, building on Signal’s own work to essentially prove the app’s encryption works. That’s a high bar for a security guarantee within the app, but it becomes meaningless if an agent can simply grab messages off a screen.

    Samsung is reportedly working on its own agent, Galaxy Claw, and Apple is developing a rival for Claude and ChatGPT as well.

    Whittaker noted Signal’s screenshot restriction isn’t perfect, saying that AI agents can still access app data through other means, “such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.” Earlier this week, a Reuters investigation supported by Signal and the AI Now Institute found that Meta’s Muse AI agent was using permissions from its initial setup in unexpected ways to access apps and data that a user had not explicitly connected it to.

    Signal remarked its protections don’t currently work on MacOS.

    “It is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” she added. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience.”.

    If you’d still like to take screenshots, you can simply disable the setting, though Signal’s announcement strongly advised against it.

    “Doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees,” Whittaker stated.

    #62417. Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1007 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people fresh tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.
    • Muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches.
    • AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people fresh tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.

    Muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches. Meta’s Muse AI agent quietly builds a profile on you the second you start using it, even if you explicitly tell it not to. That turns Jolly, its supposedly cute and cuddly mascot, into the friendly face of some serious security flaws.

    AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf. But the trade-off is privacy and control. You’re handing over your personal information to a black box with little visibility into how it’s used. Multiple incidents are fueling a conversation about the dangers of agentic AI and whether they require higher security standards before being granted access to user data.

    Recent findings suggest that that’s especially the case when it comes to handing over sensitive financial information. If you give an AI access to your digital wallets to shop for you, the risk extends beyond an authorized purchase. You could be exposing your bank accounts to a potential security breach or data exposure, with little recourse to fix it. If you were considering letting Muse make decisions and transactions with your money ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, you should know it’s still raising red flags as a shopping companion.

    Given Meta’s track record of privacy fines, data sharing and security complications, it’s worth proceeding with caution. A few months ago, a lifestyle blogger reported that the social media platform’s AI asked intrusive questions about her kids and pieced together private information about her life from her posts. Meta’s controversial smart glasses have received pushback on multiple fronts — from its facial recognition software to the way it captures and stores data.

    In a recent development, despite the risk, Muse has remained popular and now faces competition from Anthropic’s newly released Claude Duet, another AI business agent. Meta is also releasing a $300 portable device, Charm, in a virtual-toy style that will work with Muse.

    A representative for Meta has not responded to CNET’s request for comment.

    Recent findings suggest that muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

    Within weeks of launch earlier this fall, a security researcher demonstrated that the assistant could be hijacked via a zero-day exploit that Meta’s own documentation acknowledged was easy to trigger. Then, an investigative journalist discovered Muse digging through his private Apple Messages without permission. Meta disputed the claim, but Apple took it seriously enough to roll out an emergency enhancement to MacOS privacy controls.

    More recently, Meta employees themselves have flagged instances where Muse may have accessed encrypted messages from apps such as Signal or information from other Muse consumers, which Meta has chalked up to “isolated incidents” and that permission to access apps and information from notifications has to be explicitly granted in a statement to news outlets.

    If the previous incidents weren’t enough to give you pause, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

    Before facing a potential security nightmare, here are a few other things to know about Muse.

    Muse uploads iOS or Mac data even when you tell it not to: Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a September report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off. The report shows that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages. Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

    Muse could hand over data to human callers: Before Meta debuted the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the company planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments. That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

    Industry observers note that muse has the most robust data collection: In September, the VPN manufacturer Surfshark mentioned it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data. Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset of what it uncovered.

    Meta has tried hard with Muse to make the AI agent seem cute and approachable, but when it comes to your money and giving Muse access to it, it’s best to be very cautious for the time being.

    • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
    • Industry observers note that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The major day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

    If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

    Industry observers note that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

    If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, claims Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

    Industry observers note that non-electronic toys are a good bet, claims Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

    According to recent reports, neeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold says.

    While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

    According to recent reports, “Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

    Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley says.

    Got some counter space and an itch for a fresh food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

    “Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath says. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

    Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

    While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold claims.

    In a recent development, electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath says.

    According to recent reports, gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath states. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

    That stated, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold indicates.

    For best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, says consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

    You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after New Year’s Day.

    “Big-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold indicates.

    Many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

    According to recent reports, shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold claims. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

    In a recent development, just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath states. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

    One caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch says. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

    Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

    Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

    Industry observers note that fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch notes.

    Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

    Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

    Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

    It has been revealed that let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch states. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

    It has been revealed that check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley says. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

    Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    Google Is Killing the Nest App. Here’s What Comes Next

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices.
    • Sources indicate that if you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home.
    • In a recent development, all Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices.

    Sources indicate that if you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being retired, and current users will lose access to both next year.

    In a recent development, all Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

    The change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”.

    Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

    It has been revealed that google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

    As part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

    Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

    Google says that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app. Part of the goal is to give owners the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

    However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

    You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

    On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

    Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

    For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

    Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

    The other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

    The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the company starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

    Sources indicate that google says Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and customers will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

    Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

    Recent findings suggest that gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google unveiled earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. People in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

    Recent findings suggest that on your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

    10 stocks we like better than ASML ›.

    It has been revealed that the global AI expansion has created a massive demand for advanced hardware, but should you invest in the machines that print the chips or the memory that powers them? That's the choice between ASML (ASML -6.63%) and SK Hynix (SKHY -13.11%).

    Recent findings suggest that ASML provides the essential lithography systems needed to manufacture high-end logic and memory chips. SK Hynix produces the memory hardware itself, focusing on specialized high-bandwidth memory required for generative AI. Both are critical players in the global chip ecosystem, though they occupy very different niches.

    Industry observers note that ASML occupies a unique position among tech stocks because it is the sole provider of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems. These massive machines use light to print complex circuits onto silicon wafers, making them indispensable for foundries producing the latest generation of processors. The firm serves the world's largest chipmakers, though it does not disclose individual customer names in its recent SEC filings.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $43.4 billion, representing growth of 22.5% compared to the prior year. The firm reported net income of $14.8 billion during this period. This performance was supported by a strong net margin of 34.1%, which reflects its dominance in the high-end equipment market.

    In a recent development, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carries a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.2x. This ratio indicates that total debt is quite low relative to shareholder equity, indicating a conservative capital structure. Its current ratio of 1.3x measures its ability to cover short-term debts with liquid assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was $12.2 billion.

    Industry observers note that SK Hynix manufactures memory semiconductors including DRAM and NAND Flash, which are essential for data storage in everything from smartphones to data centers. The company has recently focused on high-bandwidth memory, a specialized technology that allows data to move rapidly enough for modern AI applications. While it does not disclose its largest customers in SEC filings, its products are integrated into major global electronics and server platforms.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $201.2 billion, fueled by a massive growth rate of 219.8%. Net income during this same timeframe reached $141.4 billion. This resulted in an exceptionally high net margin of 70.3%, as demand for premium AI memory products outpaced supply across the industry.

    It has been revealed that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, SK Hynix reported a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.2x. The current ratio stands at 1.9x, indicating a healthy buffer of assets available to meet upcoming financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, the company generated free cash flow of $18.5 billion, providing significant capital for further research and expansion.

    Sources indicate that ASML faces risks from geopolitical trade restrictions that limit its ability to sell advanced lithography machines to certain international markets. Because its systems are incredibly expensive and complex, the business is sensitive to the capital spending cycles of just a few massive chipmaking customers. Any significant downturn in global semiconductor demand or delays in new chip factory construction could swiftly impact its order backlog.

    SK Hynix operates in the notoriously volatile memory market, where prices for DRAM and NAND can fluctuate wildly based on global supply and demand. It faces intense competition from large rivals like Samsung and Micron, both of whom are investing heavily in competing memory technologies. Additionally, the company is exposed to regional geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions that could impact its major manufacturing hubs.

    The Forward P/E uses future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio uses sales over the past twelve months; one stock right now trades at a massive discount.

    According to recent reports, as major players in the artificial intelligence boom, ASML and SK Hynix are both attractive stocks to own. But if you had to choose one, I recommend SK Hynix. While ASML is a compelling company to invest in because it has a monopoly on EUV lithography technology, SK Hynix's share price valuation is incredibly low, while its sales are soaring.

    According to recent reports, the reason for SK Hynix's low valuation is that Wall Street is concerned the current shortage in memory chips will ease as the firm rushes to expand manufacturing capacity. Once that happens, prices and margins are likely to fall. This is typical for the cyclical nature of the computer memory industry, where boom and bust cycles are common.

    However, the AI market is expected to expand well into the 2030s. Forecasts estimate the AI industry will grow from $539.5 billion in 2026 to a whopping $9.5 trillion in 2035. This suggests SK Hynix has a multi-year tailwind to power its business. As a result, now is the time to grab shares before Wall Street realizes SK Hynix is trading at a great price.

    Even the Iconic Google Home Page Can’t Survive the Push for More AI

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This is not your parents’ Google home page.
    • The upcoming elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm.
    • The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more consumers to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of new features worldwide.

    The upcoming elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.

    The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the newly introduced buttons when signed in to my Google account.

    When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.

    Clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a new page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

    Sources indicate that clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”.

    The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.

    Another new feature, as announced by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which shows your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:.

    Stein remarked the fresh sidebar will help users go back to where they left off.

    “People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a significant difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

    I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

    Google will use your AI searches — whether they are questions, tasks, uploaded files or image generation — to train its AI models, but you can tell Google you’re opting out. CNET has an overview of how to tell chatbots not to use your data. Still, for Google specifically, you can go to Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity to turn off AI training.

    Google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google announced several other upcoming AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

    Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion consumers in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the tech giant’s “fastest growing product ever.”.

    Sources indicate that but Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The Upcoming York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts said they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

    Sources indicate that google stated search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

    It has been revealed that google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you're here looking for lower mortgage interest rates, today is definitely not your day.

    In a recent development, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points higher than yesterday and 12 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Industry observers note that keep in mind that mortgage rates are always on the move, and that if you're tracking rates day-to-day, you're going to see a lot of volatility. Zooming out and looking at the bigger picture — like a graph showing at least a month's worth of rate data — can help you see the overall trend.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    In a recent development, on Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

    The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

    Sources indicate that investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

    » MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you blueprint to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there aren’t many people for whom that’s true.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    Industry observers note that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    Recent findings suggest that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    According to recent reports, nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    In a recent development, » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    Industry observers note that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    » Stay informed: Check out NerdWallet's mortgage news hub for all our latest coverage.

    It has been revealed that the rate you see advertised is a sample rate — usually for a borrower with perfect credit, making a massive down payment, and paying for mortgage points. That won't match every buyer's circumstances.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (834 w)
    📖 Baca

    New Hyundai Elantra Hybrid Debuts With 53 Mpg, AI in the Dash

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (834 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hyundai pulled back the cover on the new 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class.
    • The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand.
    • It has been revealed that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hyundai pulled back the cover on the new 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

    The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

    It has been revealed that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

    An updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a fresh Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

    Sharing the stage in LA, the newly introduced nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

    Inside, a new cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

    Pleos Connect, Hyundai’s fresh Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is remarked to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

    The Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai notes the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

    Recent findings suggest that “Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” stated Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the upcoming Elantra is anything but bland.

    It has been revealed that the sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent new SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

    Industry observers note that the sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai claims the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

    Sources indicate that hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

    Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

    #62407. 3 High-Yield Dividend Stocks to Buy Now and 2 to Avoid Despite the Yield

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1122 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    3 High-Yield Dividend Stocks to Buy Now and 2 to Avoid Despite the Yield

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1122 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • High-yield dividend stocks often result from a falling share price.
    • Recent findings suggest that that said, there are a few diamonds in the rough, like Enterprise Products Partners (EPD -0.91%), VICI Properties (VICI +0.04%)and Verizon Communications (VZ +1.62%).
    • It has been revealed that enterprise Products Partners is a master limited partnership (MLP) that owns and operates midstream energy assets, such as oil and gas pipelines.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Thomas Niel – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:31AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vici Properties ›.

    High-yield dividend stocks often result from a falling share price. In many cases, this is a red flag. When investors bail on a dividend stock, it's typically due to falling confidence in future results. Deteriorating financial performance can, in turn, lead to dividend cuts or, worse, suspensions.

    Recent findings suggest that that said, there are a few diamonds in the rough, like Enterprise Products Partners (EPD -0.91%), VICI Properties (VICI +0.04%)and Verizon Communications (VZ +1.62%). Conversely, there are dividend stocks with such severe "yield trap" status that they are instant candidates for the "avoid" pile, like Fidelity National Information Services (FIS -0.42%) and Icahn Enterprises (IEP -7.31%).

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that enterprise Products Partners is a master limited partnership (MLP) that owns and operates midstream energy assets, such as oil and gas pipelines. Units in this MLP have a forward dividend yield of around 6.15%. Enterprise Products Partners also has a nearly 30-year track record of consecutive dividend growth.

    In a recent development, over the last decade, the MLP's quarterly payouts, known as distributions, have increased by an average of 3.6% annually. This trend appears sustainable, given the percentage of cash flow devoted not only to distributions but also to stock buybacks. Per the MLP's latest quarterly earnings release, it used just 54% of its cash flow from operations (CFFO) for return-of-capital purposes, with the remainder reinvested in the business. For comparison, most major MLPs and pipeline-owning C-corps have payout ratios of 60% and above.

    Speaking of growth, management has guided for $2.9 billion to $3.4 billion in growth-related capital spending. While not providing concrete guidance for future growth, Enterprise Products Partners has grown discretionary cash flow (DCF) from around $0.90 to $4.07 per share, or around 7.9% annualized. I wouldn't necessarily expect Enterprise to keep growing at such a clip, but even at a lesser extent, steady cash flow growth could lead to solid long-term total returns.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    VICI Properties is a real estate investment trust (REIT) specializing in casino real estate; it has since expanded to own such properties from other major gaming companies, including MGM Resorts and Golden Entertainment.

    According to recent reports, this gives REIT ownership of much of the Las Vegas Strip, as well as real estate holdings across numerous regional casino markets in the United States and overseas. VICI Properties right now has a forward dividend yield of around 7.5%. The REIT has increased its distributions for six consecutive years, with payout growth over the last five years averaging nearly 10%. Having noted this, the increase in distributions has diminished more recently. The latest dividend increase, for instance, came in at just 2.2%.

    Talk of rising interest rates has put pressure on VICI Properties, as it has on REIT stocks across the board. The pending leveraged buyout of Caesars by Fertitta Entertainment also creates some uncertainty over future rental income. Nevertheless, as the REIT continues to report solid results, including an increase in adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) per share, the REIT's equivalent of earnings per share (EPS), it remains a strong long-term choice for capital growth and a high dividend yield.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that verizon Communications is a legacy telco, built primarily from the regional Bell operating companies spun off from the old AT&T in the 1980s. Verizon's background may be what gives it its blue chip dividend stock status, but in more recent years, its legacy has been more of a liability than an asset.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, fidelity National Information Services is a leading banking and payment technology company. With a 6.6% forward dividend yield and its low valuation of just 5 times forward earnings, this fintech may at first seem like a bargain buy, but take a closer look at the reasons behind its high yield and low valuation.

    So far this year, shares have fallen by over 60%, with the stock tumbling 24% alone following its Q3 2026 earnings release earlier this month. Chalk this up to continued guidance downgrades, largely due to banks delaying their move to the tech giant's subscription-based software products. The company also has a large debt load from past acquisitions and has decided to pause buybacks to focus on deleveraging.

    The manufacturer's latest efforts have yet to lead to a dividend cut, and its payout ratio remains relatively low at around 25.7%. However, with earnings expected to drop next year and Fidelity National's history of dividend cuts, this isn't off the table. Worse yet, even if the dividend stays as is, a further deterioration in operating performance could cause the resulting stock price drop to outweigh the benefit of the company's higher-than-average yield. Until results and guidance appear more promising, consider this a "stay away" situation among dividend stocks.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Icahn Enterprises is an MLP controlled by billionaire financier Carl Icahn. However, it is not like your typical MLP that owns pipelines or other natural resource assets. Instead, it operates like a holding tech giant, with its main assets including a majority stake in refiner CVR Energy. Icahn also has holdings in other operating companies, real estate, and $1.4 billion invested in funds managed by the famed investor.

    Icahn Enterprises has long had one of the highest forward dividend yields among U.S.-listed stocks. However, its nearly 71% forward yield is very misleading. For one, Carl Icahn, who owns 87.7% of the outstanding units, receives his quarterly distributions in newly issued units, not cash. The MLP has also relied on the sale of fresh units to fund cash dividends. In other words, outside investors are trading a high yield for high shareholder dilution.

    It has been revealed that this dynamic, coupled with its recurring high investment losses and recent credit downgrade, helps to explain why this stock has lost nearly 95% of its value over the last five years. Although shares may be reaching the point where they trade below breakup value, with debt and investment loss concerns and concerns about a dividend cut persisting, a further drop appears likely.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Apple raised its prices this year, but who didn't? Well, now that Black Friday sale season is here, this is your best chance to cancel out those price hikes. That's why we're paying extra close attention to early Black Friday Apple deals.

    Sources indicate that yes, Apple does do Black Friday, but not in the way you might expect. Shopping directly on Apple's website usually means getting a measly gift card for future purchases. The real way to find great deals? Looking at retailers like Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and Target. Especially as Black Friday approaches (mark Nov. 27 in your calendar), retailers duke it out to see who can offer the best prices on AirPods, MacBooks, and iPads. Walmart and Amazon are infamous for outdoing each other by a single cent.

    Usually, prices on Apple products drop to record lows during the hectic Black Friday weekend. However, especially good deals can also sell out quick. In my five years covering Black Friday at Mashable, I've seen many an AirPod Pro deal go out of stock before I could finish writing a 200-word story about the deal.

    Industry observers note that shopping early lets you score decent savings while avoiding the post-Thanksgiving chaos. So, how do you know what to buy, and what to save for Black Friday and Cyber Monday? That's where the expertise of the Mashable shopping team can be helpful.

    Let's start with the very expensive elephant in the room. In June, Apple raised prices on MacBooks, Macs, iPads, the HomePod, Apple TVs, and even the Vision Pro headset, followed by iPhone price increases in September. With some prices rising by $200 or more, the likelihood of them falling to record lows is low. Instead, I research the market to identify products that have been at or near record lows over the past five months.

    In a recent development, I also took into account the frequency of deals. If, like the AirPods Pro 3, there's a $50 deal that's nearly always on, I don't necessarily consider that a deal worth highlighting. On the other hand, if an iPad is $100 off for the first time in a month, I'll include it and note its pricing history.

    Industry observers note that finally, I considered our reviewers' first-hand experiences with these products. Most of the items in this guide have been hands-on tested by at least one person on the Mashable staff, and I prioritized Mashable award winners, choosing the best deals based on overall product performance and value.

    In a recent development, airPods with no active noise cancellation are a thing of the past, unless you pick up a pair of the last-generation earbuds. The AirPods 4 without ANC don't stand up to the AirPods 5 with ANC at full price, but at a sub-$100 price point, they're a much better buy. With five hours of battery life per charge, an IP54 water- and dust-resistance rating, spatial audio for immersive listening, and voice isolation for calls, they're a great daily pair of earbuds. With no silicone ear tips, they're also ideal for folks who like the Apple experience, but prefer a semi-open ear design.     The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

    While this $89 sale price has been live for some time, I imagine Walmart is clearing out the last of its stock — these earbuds are no longer sold new at Amazon, Apple, or Best Buy (at least, not by a first-party seller). During Black Friday, I imagine they'll clear out for good.

    It has been revealed that the Apple AirPods Pro 3 are on sale for $179 at the time of writing. While this discount isn't necessarily bad, it is common and is almost certain to drop significantly during the week of Black Friday. Ahead of June's Prime Day sale, they dropped to a record low of $169.

If these buds are going on sale in 2026, Black Friday is likely when.

    Though not quite the lowest price we've seen for this model, it's still a great deal. According to our laptop expert, this is a great laptop for college students because of its size, but it's also a great daily driver overall. If you prefer a slightly larger display, the 15-inch Air with 1TB of storage is also $250 off at the time of writing.

If you already have a monitor, keyboard, and mouse, it's worth a look — just keep in mind that none of those come in the box.

    It has been revealed that macBook prices went up in June of this year, with the Neo jumping by $100 and the Air by $200.     Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 20, 2026

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (432 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Mashable

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Moon is now a few days past its First Quarter phase, and we're well into the Waxing Gibbous stage, which means each night, a little more of its surface is illuminated.
    • 20, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 77% of its surface visible.
    • If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis and Tranquillitatis, as well as the Kepler Crater.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Moon is now a few days past its First Quarter phase, and we're well into the Waxing Gibbous stage, which means each night, a little more of its surface is illuminated. This pattern will continue until we reach the Full Moon.

    As of Friday, Nov. 20, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 77% of its surface visible.

    If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis and Tranquillitatis, as well as the Kepler Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Posidonius Crater, the Clavius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11, 14, and 17 landing spots.

    The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

    According to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

    New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

    Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

    Sources indicate that first Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

    Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

    Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

    It has been revealed that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

    Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

    Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

    Asked on Reddit: I Lost My Job; What Should I Do First?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.
    • Recent findings suggest that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty?
    • Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

    Recent findings suggest that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

    Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

    For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

    Sources indicate that while it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any significant moves, says Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

    That’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he indicates. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

    Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

    If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, claims John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

    For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a newly introduced policy in the health insurance marketplace.

    Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your upcoming job search — is also an notable part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

    Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty states.

    “Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

    You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

    In a recent development, at the same time, it’s important to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage firm, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

    Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

    It’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a fresh park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

    Recent findings suggest that “Having that release is mentally a massive thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he states. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

    Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, indicates Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

    People often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she says.

    Starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine indicates. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

    Doing something latest also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so proposal accordingly.

    All three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

    The Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

    In a recent development, reddit is an online forum where consumers share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    #62397. With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?
