    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (803 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
    • It has been revealed that the average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
    • A mortgage is a major ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

    It has been revealed that the average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

    A mortgage is a major ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

    In a recent development, one bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

    Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

    Sources indicate that right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) highlighted consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

    Sources indicate that while CPI demonstrates how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

    Sources indicate that to cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

    It has been revealed that even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how quickly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

    Sources indicate that if you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

    In a recent development, but latest data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

    In a recent development, pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

    “Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun noted in a news release.

    It has been revealed that whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

    Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

    Industry observers note that mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

    Sources indicate that think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

    Spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

    Billionaire Investor Philippe Laffont Just Highlighted 2 Companies He Expects to Be Big Winners of the Agentic AI Era

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Philippe Laffont built his hedge fund, Coatue Management, on his ability to identify major technology trends and the companies that stand to benefit most from them ahead of the crowd.
    • In a recent development, it's easy to assert that the ability for AI agents to complete tasks for anyone could be a major transformational technology, but figuring out which companies are best positioned to profit from that transformation is a much tougher task.
    • Here's the case for both and whether the stocks are worth buying right now.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Levy – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:44AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

    Philippe Laffont built his hedge fund, Coatue Management, on his ability to identify major technology trends and the companies that stand to benefit most from them ahead of the crowd. In his latest update for investors about the outlook for the public market, he laid out a bull case for agentic AI.

    In a recent development, it's easy to assert that the ability for AI agents to complete tasks for anyone could be a major transformational technology, but figuring out which companies are best positioned to profit from that transformation is a much tougher task. Laffont doesn't leave investors hanging, though. He identified two that he views as likely winners from the agentic AI era: Meta Platforms (META -5.93%) and Intel (INTC -7.97%).

    Here's the case for both and whether the stocks are worth buying right now.

    Meta launched its Muse consumer AI agent in September, and the app saw near-instant success. It counted 10 million customers within a month and a half of its release, according to CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

    It has been revealed that laffont and his team at Coatue describe the shift from Meta's feed-based apps to Muse as a shift from monetizing attention to monetizing intent. While Meta has managed to collect huge amounts of data on its consumers that make it unparalleled at monetizing attention, explicit intent is much easier to monetize — just ask Google or Amazon.

    Industry observers note that meta's initiative is to take a small cut from every transaction that Muse processes on behalf of its people. Laffont estimates that in 2031, agentic AI commerce could account for $2.5 trillion in global gross merchandise volume. At a 10% take rate for AI agents, that's $250 billion in potential revenue, more than Meta's total revenue over the last 12 months.

    It has been revealed that meta's advertising business continues to grow as well, as advances in AI make its feeds more engaging and its ads more relevant to the people they are displayed to. That's evidenced by the increase in both price per ad and total ad impressions in each of the last 12 quarters. Coatue's analysts believe annual ad revenue per daily active user will climb from $68 this year to $153 by 2031.

    With Meta's stock trading for about 21.5 times forward earnings estimates, it looks like a bargain if it delivers that expected revenue and earnings growth. In the third quarter, Laffont increased Coatue's Meta position by 79% from the prior quarter, boosting it to 6% of the hedge fund’s public equity portfolio. The early successes of Muse could push him to buy more.

    Industry observers note that training AI requires enormous amounts of data to be handled by arrays of parallel processors — the most common of which are GPUs — and a smaller share of CPUs (central processing units). The GPU-to-CPU ratios in AI data centers built for training were recently around 8-to-1.

    However, handling the workloads for agentic AI will require servers with many more CPUs. Agentic AI processes require the systems to determine all the steps needed to complete a task and execute them in order. That's a job for a CPU, not a GPU. According to experts, data centers built for agentic AI will need to have equal numbers of GPUs and CPUS, and Laffont believes Intel is well positioned to benefit as a result.

    Sources indicate that while we've already seen the huge inflection in GPU demand, this intensifying wave of CPU demand is just getting started, Coatue's analysts argue. As more tasks are handed off to agents, CPU demand will skyrocket. They see the total addressable market for server CPUs climbing from $40 billion in 2026 to $300 billion in 2031.

    Sources indicate that of course, Intel isn't the only tech giant competing for share in server GPUs. It faces competition from several large chipmakers, including AMD, Qualcomm, Arm Holdings, and even Nvidia. Nonetheless, it's showing strong progress capitalizing on the opportunity so far, with data center revenue climbing 78% year over year in the last quarter, even as it remains supply-constrained.

    Intel holds an even larger share of the PC CPU market, which has faced challenges as a result of rising memory prices. Management expects PC unit sales to decline 20% in the second half of 2026 and another 10% in 2027. That will weigh on the company's growth until memory prices come back down, considering PC sales still account for more of Intel’s revenue than data center CPUs.

    Intel's stock price has fallen quite a bit since it peaked this summer. Laffont thinks the pullback is a buying opportunity. In the second quarter, he initiated a position of over 12 million shares for Coatue, and added 3.6 million more shares last quarter. With the stock now trading well below the price it fetched over the summer, he may be in the market to buy more. And considering the massive market opportunity ahead of the company, its current valuation of about 40 times forward earnings appears to be a fair price for the stock, even as Intel faces stiff competition in data centers and headwinds in the PC market.

    Industry News: 3 Monthly Dividend Stocks to Buy in the Financial Sector

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1119 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Main Street Capital ›.
    • Contrary to a common assumption, not every dividend stock pays its dividends quarterly.
    • Here's a closer look at three such monthly dividend payers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Main Street Capital ›.

    Contrary to a common assumption, not every dividend stock pays its dividends quarterly. Although they're relatively rare, a handful of these income-generating equity investments pay a dividend every month, better aligning with how most investors/consumers incur their recurring living expenses.

    Here's a closer look at three such monthly dividend payers. Although they're all from the financial sector and seemingly in similar businesses, each one is distinct from the other two. It wouldn't be wrong to hold a stake in all three if securing monthly dividend income is your goal right now.

    Industry observers note that main Street Capital (MAIN -1.10%) is categorized as a business development company, or BDC. That just means (as the term suggests) it helps up-and-coming organizations grow by supplying them with capital -- and, occasionally, some degree of direction. This capital can come in the form of a loan or in exchange for equity in that enterprise. Either way, as a registered BDC, Main Street Capital qualifies for certain corporate-level tax breaks, making this business structure a cost-efficient way of tapping into young companies' potential.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    You may be familiar with some of the outfits in its portfolio. Propane supplier Flame King, software company Volusion, and utility-scale radiator manufacturer Trantech are just some of the businesses that have benefited from the funding offered by Main Street Capital.

    Sources indicate that it's not an entirely consistent business. As you might imagine, the ever-changing economic backdrop pushes and pulls on its profitability, which in turn can stifle the otherwise reliable growth of its dividend payments. For instance, these payments stagnated in 2020, and in 2008 in the wake of the subprime mortgage meltdown.

    Its dividends have never gone unpaid, though, nor have they ever shrunk. You'd also be plugging into a forward-looking dividend yield of just over 8%, when including its quarterly bonus dividend in addition to its regular monthly payments.

    Recent findings suggest that between the two, Main Street Capital's total annual payout has improved from 2016's $2.73 per share to last fiscal year's $4.35. That's not bad at all, especially given the decent price gains this stock's mustered during the same 10-year time frame.

    Like Main Street Capital, Capital Southwest (CSWC -1.54%) is a business development organization, enjoying all the same tax benefits. With a forward-looking dividend yield of around 13%, however, Capital Southwest clearly does things differently than most other BDCs.

    Industry observers note that that difference -- as you might imagine -- is the risk it takes with the loans it makes. In exchange for taking on more credit risk, it requires higher interest payments, which ultimately translate into bigger dividends for shareholders. The organization's weighted average yield on its current loan portfolio is a hefty 10.9%.

    Recent findings suggest that the catch? Eventually, taking on too much risk can come back to haunt you —  like now. Technically, between last quarter's ordinary monthly dividends and its special dividend, on a per-share basis Capital Southwest dished out more in dividend payments than it actually earned. Per-share profits also fell year over year despite the increase in net investment income (a BDC's equivalent of revenue).

    That's a contributing reason why this ticker hasn't performed particularly well for the past few years, while the economic and lending environment has been hit-and-miss.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It's not catastrophic. The tech giant was still able to cover most of last quarter's dividend payment with actual earnings, as it typically does. Once interest rates and the economy stabilize, look for this BDC to once again fully fund its regular monthly dividend as well as the additional performance-based quarterly kicker.

    In the meantime, take advantage of this ticker's 10% tumble from August's peak, reflecting concerns that Capital Southwest's more aggressive lending policy isn't safe enough for this economic environment.

    Industry observers note that this organization's approach is more resilient than the market is giving it credit for, allowing you to plug into it while its yield is elevated. Just keep in mind that while the dividend yield here is phenomenal, the dividend payment barely grows from one year to the next. That's the trade-off.

    Last but not least, add Trinity Capital (TRIN -1.66%) to your list of the financial sector's monthly dividend payers to consider buying into at this time.

    Industry observers note that yes, it's yet another business development tech giant, and more like Capital Southwest than Main Street Capital. Its forward-looking dividend yield of nearly 12% reflects the above-average risk of its $2.5 billion loan and financing portfolio, with an effective interest yield of just over 15%.

    However, Trinity is different enough from Capital Southwest in a couple of key ways that owning both might still make sense. The first of these differences is where Trinity Capital's borrowers are located. Although the BDC works with plenty of domestic enterprises, it's willing and able to deploy capital overseas.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that the second of these key differences is that Trinity is more likely to exit an equity stake and move on to another opportunity than most other business development companies are. While all of them do it to some degree (out of necessity), this $1.7 billion organization sold $237 million worth of its equity investments and collected $194 million in early debt repayments last quarter alone.

    It has been revealed that this pace of turnover isn't necessarily good or bad. It's just different, underscoring how -- compared to most other business development companies -- Trinity Capital is more heavily focused on equity than on lending. This adds some diversity to whatever arrangement of monthly dividend payers you're eyeing.

    Recent findings suggest that with that being remarked, you should know that Trinity hasn't raised its annualized dividend since 2024. This doesn't mean it will never happen again. It just means you can't count on it every year, if you know you need it.

    Even so, with such a high yield at the same time this ticker's moved measurably higher since this bull market took hold in 2023, a stagnant monthly dividend payment may still be worth it.

    This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1478 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    According to recent reports, if you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    Industry observers note that you can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    Recent findings suggest that stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    There are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    Recent findings suggest that if you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    According to recent reports, for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    It has been revealed that for a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    The family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    Next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    One of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    It has been revealed that if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    • IonQ (IONQ -8.76%) is an intriguing stock.
    • IonQ is the biggest pure-play quantum computing investment available on the market, and its business continues to grow rapidly as demand for early-stage quantum computers arrives.
    • According to recent reports, so, is now the perfect time to buy?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than IonQ ›.

    IonQ (IONQ -8.76%) is an intriguing stock. It hasn't done well in 2026 and is down nearly 50% this year and down around 70% from its all-time high. On the surface, that doesn't look promising. However, once investors wrap their heads around what is going on, it starts to look much more inviting.

    IonQ is the biggest pure-play quantum computing investment available on the market, and its business continues to grow rapidly as demand for early-stage quantum computers arrives. But with the market seemingly not caring about this growth, the stock is cheap.

    According to recent reports, so, is now the perfect time to buy? I think so, as the market could care less about quantum computing right now.

    Sources indicate that ionQ is a pure-play quantum computing company, meaning it doesn't have any other businesses to fund its operations. So, it must produce a viable quantum computer or risk going bankrupt. That's a high-risk scenario, but the rewards will be immense if IonQ can pull it off.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, the market selling off IonQ's stock during 2026 has little to do with how it's actually doing as a firm. Instead, it is more of a reflection of the market's risk appetite. Investors have gotten wary of investing in higher-risk investments during 2026. AI is generally considered a lower risk than quantum computing because there's actually usable technology in that sector. So, with quantum computing being an even riskier segment than that, the market has heavily sold it off.

    However, I think that makes the timing right to buy IonQ stock, as the time to buy is when there is no fanfare around the industry.

    Recent findings suggest that ionQ has been making great strides toward becoming a viable business. Next year, its 256-qubit Superion system releases, which will be one of the most powerful early-stage quantum computers available. It has several clients that have already preordered, and with $1.2 billion in revenue backlog, there is monster demand for this product.

    Recent findings suggest that however, IonQ isn't just focused on developing a viable quantum computer. Earlier this year, it acquired SkyWater, which is a semiconductor foundry. This helps decrease development time for IonQ and also gives it more control over its supply chain.

    It also acquired Elisity, which will help IonQ pioneer quantum-focused cybersecurity. All of these moves were made to make IonQ a one-stop shop for all things quantum computing-related. It is a bold strategy and could turn it into the next tech giant if it works out, but there's no guarantee of success.

    Investors must understand and manage risk with IonQ, as it is far from a surefire investment.

    It has been revealed that ionQ isn't the only tech giant competing in this space. There are countless others, including several well-funded big tech companies. IonQ is also taking a different technological approach that prioritizes accuracy over computing speed. This may be an advantage in the early stages of quantum computing, as accuracy is one of the primary concerns for people. But if companies with faster processing speeds catch up to IonQ's accuracy levels, then IonQ could be in trouble.

    In a recent development, the question of whether IonQ turns into a successful manufacturer pivots around how promptly it can launch its commercially viable quantum computer and how much of a head start (if any) it has on its competitors. That will determine the investing success of IonQ, and there's no way of knowing for sure if it will even reach the commercially viable state.

    Sources indicate that as a result, if you're going to invest in IonQ, then keeping position sizing small (say 1%) is a smart idea. I think IonQ is an excellent long-shot investment opportunity, but only if you have the mindset that this stock is more of a lottery ticket right now.

    Eli Lilly's Next Massive Growth Opportunity Could Be Hiding in Plain Sight

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:17PM EST.
    • In a recent development, eli Lilly (LLY -0.30%) delivered yet another impressive earnings report last month.
    • Zepbound is right now approved for weight loss for adults aged 18 and older, provided their BMI (Body Mass Index) is at least 30 or at least 27 with a weight-related comorbidity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:17PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Eli Lilly ›.

    In a recent development, eli Lilly (LLY -0.30%) delivered yet another impressive earnings report last month. The manufacturer's third-quarter upgrade indicated that its core growth drivers, including Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for weight loss, don't seem anywhere close to running out of steam. The best part is that Eli Lilly is actively looking to tap into new market niches, and some of the company's recent clinical trial results could open another vital opportunity. Let's look into it.

    Zepbound is right now approved for weight loss for adults aged 18 and older, provided their BMI (Body Mass Index) is at least 30 or at least 27 with a weight-related comorbidity. It isn't indicated for anyone younger than that. But Eli Lilly has been running clinical studies to test whether Zepbound is effective in younger patients. It recently reported results from one of those trials.

    Recent findings suggest that the study in question enrolled people aged 12 to 17. Half of them had obesity-related complications, while 75% met the threshold for class 2 or class 3 severe obesity. During the study, participants who received Zepbound lost an average of about 40 pounds, while those receiving a placebo gained an average of 5 pounds after 72 weeks.

    According to recent reports, also, BMI decreased by 18.5% in patients who took Zepbound, compared with a 0.5% increase in the placebo group. Further, Zepbound led to improvements in various measures, including LDL cholesterol and triglycerides (which are linked to increased cardiovascular risk), as well as improved quality of life.

    Recent findings suggest that safety data were consistent with what we know about GLP-1 drugs. These results could help support a label expansion for Zepbound in younger patients.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that there are about 25.6 million people between 12 and 17 years of age in the U.S. The prevalence of obesity among people aged 2 to 19 has been about 21% in recent years, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Applying that to the 12- to 17-year-old population, we get a potential market of more than five million patients -- a significant opportunity.

    And that's only in the U.S. Assuming Eli Lilly can generate about $6,000 in net revenue per patient and the pharmaceutical company reaches 20% penetration in this population, we are talking about an additional annual net revenue of about $6.5 billion.

    Note that in the third quarter, Zepbound generated $5.4 billion in revenue, up 49% year over year. Eli Lilly's total revenue grew 39% year over year to $24.4 billion. An additional $6.5 billion in annual sales from Zepbound would therefore be meaningful. Of course, there are important caveats to consider.

    For one, it will take time for Eli Lilly to ramp up Zepbound sales in this niche. Also, Eli Lilly will face competition in this market. The firm's biggest challenger, Novo Nordisk (NVO -2.70%), has earned approval for its famous GLP-1 drug, Wegovy, in this patient population.

    Third, Eli Lilly's net realized prices might decline as more weight loss drugs enter the market. Even with these caveats, this opportunity looks potentially highly lucrative for Eli Lilly. The company has proven that Zepbound is more effective than Wegovy. And given the benefits Zepbound demonstrated in adolescents beyond weight loss, it should attract a significant share of that market, even with increased competition. However, does this make Eli Lilly stock a buy?

    The potential label expansion for Zepbound in adolescents appears attractive, and it once again highlights Eli Lilly's strength in one of its core therapeutic areas. Eli Lilly is also running clinical trials for Zepbound in patients between six and 11 years of age, which could add more than five million patients to its addressable market, provided the medicine proves effective in this study.

    In a recent development, and we haven't even mentioned the several other clinical trial candidates the firm has in weight loss or, for that matter, the deep pipeline it has built in other therapeutic areas, such as oncology. So, Eli Lilly's prospects look attractive. The stock has outperformed broader equities this year -- and since the turn of the decade, for that matter -- but there may be plenty of upside left.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to upcoming inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Industry observers note that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    In a recent development, if PCE reveals inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    Sources indicate that I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index revealed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    In a recent development, » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a latest home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1402 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • Industry observers note that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's vital to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • Sources indicate that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    Industry observers note that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's vital to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    Sources indicate that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    Industry observers note that these scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    It has been revealed that some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s notable to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    Industry observers note that merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    Sources indicate that merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    In a recent development, merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    In a recent development, some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that shows more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Industry observers note that unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    According to recent reports, some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    It has been revealed that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    It has been revealed that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    Industry observers note that scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    Sources indicate that which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    Recent findings suggest that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    The best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    It has been revealed that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    Apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a big impact when you add several of them together.

    According to recent reports, understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    Not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    Warren Buffett Noted Stocks Are Better Than Bonds for Long-Term Investors. History Demonstrates He Was Right.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF ›.
    • Sources indicate that warren Buffett became a legendary investor by investing in stocks, not bonds.
    • Many people think of bonds as being "less risky" than stocks, and that can be true.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Ben Gran – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF ›.

    Sources indicate that warren Buffett became a legendary investor by investing in stocks, not bonds. But he had some strong opinions about bonds that other investors should consider.

    Many people think of bonds as being "less risky" than stocks, and that can be true. But understanding the "risk" of bonds vs. stocks depends on your time horizon and investment goals.

    In his 2017 shareholder letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, Warren Buffett shared an interesting story about his experience with the true risks of bonds. This experience reminded him why he prefers buying stocks.

    Let's look at why Buffett noted that stocks are a better buy than bonds for most long-term investors.

    It has been revealed that in 2017, Buffett was reaching the end of a unique, public 10-year-long wager. He had made a friendly bet with an investment advisory firm, Protégé Partners, to see if professional hedge fund managers could outperform the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) for the next 10 years, starting in 2008.

    Buffett bet that they couldn't. He believed that most professional money managers would fail to beat the S&P 500 for that long.

    Sources indicate that buffett was right. All five of the professional hedge fund managers chosen by Protégé failed to beat the S&P 500.

    The bet involved $1 million, with Buffett and Protégé each pledging $500,000 toward that total. No matter who won the bet, the $1 million proceeds would go to a Nebraska charity, Girls Inc. of Omaha.

    In a recent development, to fund the bet, Buffett and Protégé each bought a package of zero-coupon U.S. Treasury bonds worth $318,250 when purchased at the start of the bet (about 64% of face value) and would be worth $500,000 after 10 years (for a total of $1 million at the end of the bet).

    According to recent reports, but midway through the bet, in 2012, Buffett realized that due to recent changes in the bond market, their zero-coupon Treasury bonds had become a terrible investment. The bonds had started out yielding about 4.56% annually, but by 2012, with five years left until maturity, they were yielding only about 0.88% annually.

    Industry observers note that warren Buffett can't abide a bad deal on an investment. He and Protégé quickly agreed to sell their Treasury bonds and put the proceeds into Berkshire Hathaway (BRKB -0.36%) Class B shares. He was confident that Berkshire Hathaway stock would deliver a much better average annual return for the next five years than 0.88%.

    Once again, he was right. As a result, as Buffett wrote: "Girls Inc. of Omaha found itself receiving $2,222,279 last month rather than the $1 million it had originally hoped for.".

    Buffett's experience with Treasury bonds taught a few notable lessons about the real risks of bond investing. Here are a few reasons, according to Buffett, why bonds can be riskier than stocks:.

    Buffett wrote that investing is about giving up consumption today so you can have more money to spend later. But bonds can fail to achieve this goal if they don't make your money grow in the long run.

    As he wrote, "By that standard, purportedly 'risk-free' long-term bonds in 2012 were a far riskier investment than a long-term investment in common stocks.".

    Recent findings suggest that if inflation is 3% per year and bonds deliver 4% yields, they're barely staying ahead of inflation. Buffett bought those zero-coupon Treasury bonds at a time of lower inflation and lower interest rates than we have today. But from 2012 to 2017, his bonds were on track to yield only 0.88% per year.

    Buffett noted this inflation risk of bonds when he wrote: "At that time, even a 1% annual rate of inflation between 2012 and 2017 would have decreased the purchasing-power of the government bond that Protégé and I sold.".

    Industry observers note that the S&P 500 can crash on any given day, but it tends to go up in the long run. That means the longer your time horizon, the longer you can hold your stocks, and the more likely they’ll deliver a positive return. Bonds can be safer than stocks in the short run, but over time, stocks gradually become a better bet.

    Industry observers note that as Buffett wrote: "...in any upcoming day, week, or even year, stocks will be riskier -- far riskier -- than short-term U.S. bonds. As an investor's investment horizon lengthens, however, a diversified portfolio of U.S. equities becomes progressively less risky than bonds, assuming that the stocks are purchased at a sensible multiple of earnings relative to then-prevailing interest rates.".

    In a recent development, buffett followed up on these ideas in his shareholder letter in a February 2018 interview with CNBC, where he noted he believed long-term investors should buy stocks rather than bonds. He said, "If you had to choose between buying long-term bonds or equities, I would choose equities in a minute...If I were going to own a 30-year government bond or own equities for 30 years, I think equities will considerably outperform that 30-year bond.".

    In a recent development, history demonstrates that Warren Buffett was right. In the eight years since Buffett's shareholder letter and CNBC interview in Feb. 2018, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) has strongly outperformed the Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF (BND +0.59%).

    BND Total Return Level data by YCharts.

    This doesn't mean you shouldn't buy any bonds. Bond ETFs can be appropriate as part of a diversified portfolio. Today's bonds offer higher yields than they did when Buffett was buying Treasury bonds in 2008, which could make them a better deal for investors than they used to be. I own shares of the Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF, even though my time horizon for investing is still decades long.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But if you want maximum growth of your money and can hold for the long term through short-term stock market booms and busts, buying stocks should be the foundation of your investment strategy.

    Airbnb is known for having sizable stock-based compensation, totaling $1.4 billion over the last nine months. This is how businesses, particularly those earlier in their life cycles, pay their employees. But it results in an increase in the share count.

    In a recent development, to Airbnb's credit, though, its outstanding share count shrank by almost 3% in the past year. The company conducted $4 billion in stock buybacks over the last 12 months. Combining the latest $12 billion repurchase authorization with the $2.7 billion remaining capacity means Airbnb now intends to buy 12% of the company's entire market capitalization.

    In a recent development, investors benefit from this tailwind. A smaller outstanding share count provides a jolt to earnings per share (EPS). Shareholders who continue to hold the stock see their ownership percentage in the business increase over time.

    The best companies can balance returning capital to investors with reinvesting into their operations. Airbnb is certainly still playing offense.

    The business continues to expand its list of services. Travelers can now book hotels. And there are more active partnerships in place. And for hosts, a redesigned calendar makes juggling multiple listings far simpler.

    Airbnb is also leaning into the opportunity that artificial intelligence (AI) presents. It looks to release an AI-powered travel assistant in 2027.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    For context, in fiscal 2026 (ended Sept. 26), Apple (AAPL -1.90%) produced $136.1 billion in FCF, a mind-boggling figure. Its FCF margin was 28%, however, which is lower than Airbnb’s FCF margin.

    Hats off to Airbnb's asset-light business model. The tech giant doesn't own the properties listed on its platform, eliminating the need for a sizable investment. And that frees up cash for repurchasing shares.

    This leads to the next point, which concerns the wide economic moat Airbnb has built since its founding in 2007. The firm benefits from a powerful global network effect. It's a positive feedback loop in which more guest bookings attract more hosts to try to make money from their listings. In turn, the wider selection leads to a better, more compelling experience for travelers.

    The fear that AI agents will handle the entire booking process for consumers and challenge this favorable position is warranted. However, Airbnb's advantage as the middleman comes from convenience, trust, and centralized tools it offers to both guests and hosts. The strong Q3 financial figures prove there is no cause for alarm yet.

    "As we build Airbnb to become an AI-native manufacturer, I actually think the opportunity ahead of us is actually even bigger," co-founder and chief executive officer Brian Chesky stated on the Q3 2026 earnings call.

    According to recent reports, airbnb is worth keeping an eye on, provided you're an investor searching for high-quality stocks to own for five years or more. It's a compounding machine. Consensus analyst estimates call for EPS to grow at an annualized rate of 24% from fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2028.

    Sources indicate that because shares trade at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 29.7, much of the good news is already reflected. Know this before you make a move.

    Recent findings suggest that so now is an excellent time for equity investors of all stripes to understand that Fed actions affect various sectors in different ways. For example, the capital-intensive, debt-heavy utility sector is often vulnerable to higher borrowing costs when rates rise. In contrast, higher rates are seen as boons to financial services stocks due to net interest margin expansion.

    Energy stocks have also shown strength as rates rise, suggesting that exchange-traded funds (ETFs) such as the Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE -0.73%) are worth considering ahead of the next Fed meeting and beyond.

    #62374. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1033 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • Industry observers note that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    Industry observers note that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    In a recent development, the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," stated Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone stated.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That noted, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, said Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    Sources indicate that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she remarked.

    The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, mentioned Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he said. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    According to recent reports, in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she noted.

    Industry observers note that "It is isolated," she remarked. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    In a recent development, but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin mentioned. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    In a recent development, it's also crucial to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, stated R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

    "That's when spreads really widen out," he said. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    That stated, Nvidia's data center segment now represents 93% of its revenue, making the firm exceptionally vulnerable to a drop in data center demand.

    It has been revealed that the market could weaken because of regulatory changes. Many Democratic lawmakers are already pledging to push back on data center construction. Rising interest rates could also pose a problem, as they make it more expensive for clients to raise the debt capital needed to purchase large volumes of chips. There is also the risk that demand on the customer-facing side of the AI industry will not be sufficient to justify the substantial spending on AI infrastructure.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Ryan Vanzo – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:27PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Many of the world's most valuable companies today are artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. That's for good reason. The global AI opportunity is truly massive, and many AI hyperscalers are already quite profitable. But what will happen to these companies during a market crash?

    Only around 10% of the S&P 500's value is tied directly to companies engaged in developing AI software. However, between 40% and 50% of the index's value is indirectly exposed to AI. That includes major GPU producers such as Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), as well as AI-enabled software providers like Palo Alto Networks and ServiceNow.

    In short, if markets fall, there's a very strong chance AI stocks will lead the way. It would be no surprise to see AI stocks struggle in a market downturn. While high growth rates may support premium valuations, companies with high growth rates already priced into shares typically falter as markets rerate risk tolerances. But as a recent report from BlackRock points out:.

    According to recent reports, if market sentiment becomes risk-averse, pressuring AI stock valuations, investors would be wise to peruse the bargain bin for deals. There's one AI stock I'm keeping a very close eye on, as its underlying fundamentals and already cheap valuation should make it a strong buy during a market crash.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    During market crashes or economic downturns, companies with strong fundamentals often have an opportunity to grow stronger. That's because weaker competitors may face financial difficulties and exit the market. Acquisition prices get cheaper, with expansion opportunities facing less competition.

    When conducting a meta-analysis of firms entering a downturn with strong financials and end-market demand, McKinsey & Co. found that these businesses "emerged much stronger coming out of the downturn, and the advantage they gained lasted for a long period.".

    With this in mind, it's not hard to see Nvidia as a strong choice -- perhaps the strongest choice -- for investors during a market downturn. There is no denying that Nvidia's core business is exposed to long-term growth tailwinds. Both sales and earnings are currently growing at roughly 100% year over year. Growth rates should reach 50% to 100% annually over the coming years.

    According to recent reports, GPUs are critical components for the AI revolution. Even if Nvidia's leadership position weakens, resulting in lower market shares and compressed margins, top-line growth should remain in the double digits throughout the rest of the decade, perhaps even longer.

    Recent headwinds, however -- including an abrupt and controversial CEO transition, potential regulatory pressures, and allegations of circular financing -- have pushed Nvidia's price-to-earnings ratio down to just 16.2, with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of just 9.6.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia generated $43 billion in free cash flow last quarter. And the organization currently has $227 billion remaining on an upscaled share repurchase initiative.

    It has been revealed that despite near-term concerns, Nvidia remains a financial powerhouse that manufactures critical components essential to the AI industry's expansion. In the event of a downturn, the firm can repurchase shares at a discount, reinvest heavily in research and development, and acquire competitors at bargain prices.

    It's not clear how much cheaper Nvidia shares can get from here. The organization's current fundamentals and near-term growth forecasts already make shares a buy. If a marketwide downturn hits, however, many longer-term concerns, such as eventual margin compression, may become fully priced into shares.

    In a recent development, there's still a lot we don't know about Nvidia's future, especially in today's environment. But what we do know is that the tech giant is completely self-funded; benefits from strong, secular growth tailwinds; and has the financial might to outinvest and perhaps even outright acquire much of its competition, barring the internal divisions of hyperscalers.

    It has been revealed that I'm already strongly considering an investment in Nvidia. Oddly enough, a market downturn could actually strengthen that conviction.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The neocloud had to delay the delivery of some new capacity due to issues with a third-party provider. That wasn’t Nebius' fault, and the company is building its future data centers to avoid third-party risk moving forward. The end result is that Nebius says it will not hit the $7 billion annual recurring revenue (ARR) target it forecast for December until February.

    It has been revealed that anyone who is holding Nebius stock is doing so for the long run. While this two-month delay ruined short-term call options, it didn't affect the long-term thesis much. Artificial intelligence is still heating up, with demand scaling upward.

    Industry observers note that financing and profitability have been among the main concerns people have about the neocloud, but Nebius squashed them both in its third-quarter shareholder letter. Its fresh contracts provide prepayments that cover all capital expenditures. Furthermore, the company expects to be breaking even on a pre-tax basis by 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that within five to 10 years, it's possible that the conversation will shift from Nebius raising money to management initiating stock buybacks. It's quite feasible, since the manufacturer's payback period for newly introduced data centers has dropped to one year and seven months, and that excludes prepayments.

    Its annual contract value per megawatt now exceeds $25 million for long-term deals, and Nebius wasted no time mentioning key enterprise AI leaders that recently became latest customers.

    Nebius believes it can generate $12 billion to $13 billion in ARR by the end of 2027. Granted, unforeseen delays could push some of that revenue out into 2028, as investors witnessed when Nebius said it wouldn’t reach its $7 billion ARR target until February.

    According to recent reports, importantly, though, that guidance reveals that growth is not slowing down. In Q3, Nebius delivered 571% year-over-year revenue growth to $981 million. That was also a 68% sequential growth rate from the second quarter.

    According to recent reports, nebius has remarked that it expects to be operating at breakeven on a pre-tax basis by the end of 2027, and that its data centers are recouping the capital investments required to bring them online in just 19 months. However, that's still underselling Nebius as an investment.

    One key detail investors may be overlooking is how negotiations will change when it's time to renew contracts. Nebius has to negotiate prepayments to fund its data centers. Receiving capital up front makes it more viable to build data centers at scale.

    In a recent development, customers make prepayments in exchange for lower annual contract values for each megawatt. Once Nebius operates data centers that have been fully paid off, it won't be as reliant on prepayments. That will give Nebius the flexibility to set higher prices per megawatt, and the soaring demand for compute implies that the elevated prices will stick.

    According to recent reports, nebius revealed in its Q2 shareholder letter that it gets annual contract values of $40 million to $50 million per megawatt for short-term deals. Customers aren't afraid of those prices, and long-term deals may get closer to those levels once prepayments are no longer necessary.

    Industry observers note that this detail, combined with Nebius' current performance and pipeline, suggests it can produce 100% or higher year-over-year revenue growth for multiple years.
