    #62352. The S&P 500 Heads Into Thanksgiving Below Its Peak. Here's How the Holiday Week Has Usually Gone Since 1950.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (864 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    The S&P 500 Heads Into Thanksgiving Below Its Peak. Here's How the Holiday Week Has Usually Gone Since 1950.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) finished on Nov.
    • Chipmakers were among the worst hit that day, amid worries that the midterm election results might slow the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out.
    • The market is closed on Thursday, Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:47PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Industry observers note that the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) finished on Nov. 16 at 7,416.59, around 5% under the all-time closing high of 7,818.93 it set on Oct. 6. The drop sped up in late October, and the index fell over 4% on Nov. 5 alone as tech stocks sold off.

    Chipmakers were among the worst hit that day, amid worries that the midterm election results might slow the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out.

    The market is closed on Thursday, Nov. 26, for Thanksgiving, and it closes early (at 1 p.m. ET) the next day.

    According to recent reports, historically, this has been a better-than-average week to hold stocks. Since 1950, the index has climbed during Thanksgiving week in 53 of 76 years, or about 70% of the time, and the week's average gain has been roughly 0.7%. By comparison, normal weeks across the same stretch rose 56% of the time and gained roughly 0.2% on average.

    According to recent reports, but the record looks weaker in years like this one. In the 13 years the index entered the week 3% to 10% under a recent record close, it rose in just seven.

    Recent findings suggest that I measured each year from the close on the Friday before Thanksgiving to the close on the Friday after, with the index's daily closes from Yahoo Finance (which count price moves only, not dividends). That normally includes four trading sessions around the holiday.

    Recent findings suggest that notably, the gains haven't been spread evenly among them. Monday and Tuesday combined averaged a gain of only about 0.1% and finished up in 47 of the 76 years. The Wednesday before Thanksgiving, though, climbed in 58 years and averaged a gain of around 0.3%. The Friday after climbed in 54, with an average gain close to that.

    So, the two sessions on either side of the holiday make up almost all the week's typical gain.

    The range has been wide, too. The best Thanksgiving week came in 2008, in the middle of the financial crisis, when the index jumped about 12% from around half its record. The worst was 2011, with a loss of nearly 5%.

    Industry observers note that to match this year's setup, I looked for weeks that began with the index at least 3% but no more than 10% below its record close, with that record set within around four months. Thirteen years qualified, from 1951 to 2025.

    The week rose in seven of them, and the average gain was around 0.4%. That's still a little better than a regular week. But it's around half the average for all 76 Thanksgiving weeks, and the hit rate drops from about 70% to about 54%.

    The two latest cases went in opposite directions. In 2018, the index began the week around 7% below its September record and dropped nearly 4% more -- and by Dec. 31, it was about 8% below where it started the week.

    Last year, it came in about 4% under its Oct. 28 record and climbed nearly 4%.

    Also, the rest of the year was better for the group. In 10 of these 13 years, the index closed the year above its level on the Friday before Thanksgiving. Out of all 76 years, the same was true for 54.

    For anyone owning an S&P 500 index fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%), the next 12 months may matter more than the next four sessions. Twelve of the 13 cases have a full year of data after them, and a year after the Friday before Thanksgiving, the index was up in six and down in six.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    These years ranged from a rise of around 24% after 1963 to a drop of about 40% after 2007.

    In 2007, the holiday week cost the index only about 1%. But the October record turned out to be the peak before a bear market that cut the index by over half. And 2018's bad week came before a rise of 14% over the next year.

    Sure, 13 years is a small sample, and the fall from a 70% hit rate to 54% could easily be chance.

    In a recent development, the Vanguard fund finished Nov. 16 around $680, about 5% under the $718.47 peak it hit within the last year.

    Industry observers note that I think the holiday week's history is a slight edge in investors' favor, and one that has mostly faded in years when the index started below a record. For a long-term owner of the fund, that isn't much to act on either way.

    Breaking: Better Buy: Bitcoin vs. Ethereum

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bitcoin (BTC +2.43%) and Ether (ETH +4.36%) are the world's two most valuable cryptocurrencies.
    • Sources indicate that bitcoin, which reached $126,000 last October, is now worth roughly $60,000.
    • In the past, Bitcoin and Ether were both mined using the energy-intensive proof-of-work (PoW) consensus mechanism, in which miners used powerful computing hardware to solve cryptographic puzzles and earn tokens as rewards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Leo Sun – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:55PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

    Bitcoin (BTC +2.43%) and Ether (ETH +4.36%) are the world's two most valuable cryptocurrencies. But after setting record highs in 2025, both tokens tumbled in 2026.

    Sources indicate that bitcoin, which reached $126,000 last October, is now worth roughly $60,000. Ether, which topped $4,950 last August, trades at about $1,700. Let's see why these top "blue chip" cryptocurrencies crumbled -- and if either one is worth buying in this choppy market.

    In the past, Bitcoin and Ether were both mined using the energy-intensive proof-of-work (PoW) consensus mechanism, in which miners used powerful computing hardware to solve cryptographic puzzles and earn tokens as rewards.

    CRYPTO · As of 4:40 PM ET 11/21/26.

    But there was a key difference: Bitcoin was primarily designed as a digital commodity, while Ethereum (the blockchain behind Ether) was built to support complex smart contracts, which are used to develop decentralized apps and tokenized assets. Bitcoin supported only simple smart contracts, and its limited programmability made it less attractive to developers.

    Industry observers note that in 2022, the Ethereum network -- whose native token is Ether -- transitioned to the more energy-efficient proof-of-stake (PoS) consensus mechanism. Under PoS, validators stake (lock up) their Ether tokens to help secure the network and validate transactions, earning rewards for their participation rather than simply mining new tokens. The bigger Ethereum's developer ecosystem grows, the more valuable Ether -- which funds the "gas fees" for those transactions -- becomes.

    CRYPTO · As of 4:34 PM ET 11/21/26.

    Today, Ether's value is closely tied to Ethereum's developer growth, while Bitcoin's value is still driven by its scarcity, utility, and value to institutional investors. Bitcoin has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens. More than 20 million of those tokens have already been mined, and its blockchain undergoes a "halving" every four years to cut its mining rewards in half.

    In a recent development, ether doesn't have a fixed maximum supply, and it fluctuates between being an inflationary token and a deflationary one based on Ethereum's network activity. Ethereum is upgrading its network to make it more scalable and secure, but it also faces intense competition from faster PoS blockchains like Solana (SOL +2.71%) and Cardano (ADA +3.58%). To stay ahead of these competitors, Ethereum is supporting more Layer 2 (L2) applications that bundle together transactions and process them off-chain at higher speeds than its Layer 1 (L1) blockchain.

    Recent findings suggest that bitcoin and Ether have more long-term catalysts than many other smaller altcoins, but they aren't immune to the macro headwinds for the broader crypto market. Last year, many crypto investors expected interest rate cuts, clearer, crypto-friendly regulations, and lower Treasury yields to drive investors back toward cryptocurrencies and riskier investments.

    But the opposite happened. The Iran war exacerbated inflation, driving the Fed to raise its rates for the first time in three years. Treasury yields spiked, and the CLARITY Act -- which would have provided a clearer regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies -- died in the Senate.

    Recent findings suggest that the Democratic sweep of the U.S. midterm elections also suggests that more restrictive regulations could be passed against the crypto industry. All of those challenges chilled the crypto market and drove investors toward safer, higher-yielding investments again.

    Bitcoin and Ether will both remain under pressure for the foreseeable future. But if I had to pick one over the other, I'd buy Bitcoin because it has more growth potential as a hedge against expansionary monetary policies and the debasement of fiat currencies. Once its price stabilizes, it could become more comparable to "digital gold" than other cryptocurrencies.

    Ether also has a bright future as the "digital oil" of decentralized applications. Still, that future is murkier due to intense competition from Solana, Cardano, and other PoS blockchains with faster transactions and lower fees. Unless Ether widens its moat against those competitors, it could have less upside potential than Bitcoin when the crypto winter finally ends.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By John Ballard – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Amazon ›.

    Sticking with familiar brands and services is one of the best ways for the average investor to pick winning stocks. A stock's price tends to follow its earnings over time. A company growing earnings at least 15% a year can double in five years, and some of the most dominant consumer services can still achieve that level of growth.

    Wall Street expects the following top growth stocks to deliver 19% or better annual earnings growth, putting a double by 2031 within reach.

    Amazon (AMZN -4.10%)shares closed at $257.89 on Nov. 17, up 11% over the past year and 45% over the past five years, trailing the S&P 500's 56% five-year return. The reason it can double by 2031 is expanding margins, which the market hasn't fully priced in yet.

    Industry observers note that over the past three years, Amazon's trailing-12-month operating income has risen 283% to $106 billion. Amazon's most profitable business is its cloud services segment. Still, it has many levers to increase profitability from growth in other non-retail services, which make up the majority of its $797 billion in annual revenue.

    Advertising is a profitable business to watch. Amazon sells ads to brands and sellers that want to reach its shoppers. Ad revenue grew 12% year over year on a constant-currency basis to $19.6 billion in the third quarter, bringing it close to $80 billion annually.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    However, that growth doesn't show the real momentum. Moving Prime Day into Q2 cut 8.5 percentage points from Q3 ad growth, according to CEO Andy Jassy. Excluding currency swings, ad sales grew 22% to 26% in each of the five prior quarters, and management expects ad growth to return to the high teens in Q4.

    Recent findings suggest that amazon trades at about 27 times forward earnings, which is reasonable given analysts' expectations that earnings will grow about 24% per year over the coming years. If the valuation multiple holds, and Amazon delivers on those expectations, the stock could more than double by 2031.

    According to recent reports, airbnb (ABNB -1.41%)shares closed at $180.94 on Nov. 17, up 54% over the past year but down 9% over the past five years. The business has continued to grow, creating a good buying opportunity.

    Management states "Airbnb is back in growth mode." Q3 revenue rose 19% year over year, its fastest growth in more than three years, and management raised its full-year outlook.

    Latest products are driving the momentum. Airbnb shipped more than 50 products and features in the quarter, nearly 70% more than a year earlier, and states artificial intelligence (AI) is helping its teams move faster.

    Its own AI travel agent starts rolling out in the first half of 2027. CEO Brian Chesky wants AI built into the way the firm works, and he has described AI tools as a superpower for running it. This spells faster updates for its platform, more efficient operations, and the potential for strong earnings growth.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Analysts expect Airbnb's earnings to grow about 19% a year over the long term. That is enough to double the share price, assuming the stock still trades at the same forward earnings multiple of 32. Chesky said that as it becomes an AI-native company, "the opportunity ahead of us is actually even bigger.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, medtronic (MDT -0.67%), one of the world's largest medical device makers, will post its next earnings report on Nov.
    • According to recent reports, in fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024 (which ended in April 2024), Medtronic's earnings declined as it struggled with supply chain constraints, inflation, forex headwinds, regulatory challenges for its diabetes business, and lumpy post-pandemic recovery in elective procedures.
    • It has been revealed that but in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026, its earnings grew again as it stabilized its costs, expanded its higher-growth cardiovascular and neuroscience businesses, and spun off MiniMed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Leo Sun – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:07PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Medtronic ›.

    According to recent reports, medtronic (MDT -0.67%), one of the world's largest medical device makers, will post its next earnings report on Nov. 24. It will mark its first earnings report after it spun off its diabetes unit, MiniMed (MMED -1.54%), and fully removed its business from its balance sheet.

    According to recent reports, in fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024 (which ended in April 2024), Medtronic's earnings declined as it struggled with supply chain constraints, inflation, forex headwinds, regulatory challenges for its diabetes business, and lumpy post-pandemic recovery in elective procedures. Tougher competition, quality control issues, and latest GLP-1 drugs exacerbated that pressure.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that but in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026, its earnings grew again as it stabilized its costs, expanded its higher-growth cardiovascular and neuroscience businesses, and spun off MiniMed. In fiscal 2026, its revenue grew 5.8% organically, marking its strongest top-line growth in a decade. For fiscal 2027, it expects its revenue to rise another 7.25%-7.75%.

    Recent findings suggest that for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, analysts expect Medtronic's revenue to rise 6% year over year but for its adjusted EPS to dip 2%. Its cardiovascular and neuroscience businesses should remain strong. Still, the completion of its MiniMed spin-off (which concluded on Oct. 15), its reinvestment in higher-growth platforms, early-stage manufacturing costs for newer cardiovascular devices, and a few recent acquisitions are squeezing its margins.

    In a recent development, medtronic's stock looks cheap at 17 times forward earnings and pays a forward yield of 2.9%. However, I'd wait to see how well it grows organically -- and how it's handling the margin pressure -- before buying the stock and assuming it's a safe blue chip dividend play.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a tech giant's ability to pay dividends consistently.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a tech giant's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Industry observers note that integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The company has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    It has been revealed that in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Industry observers note that specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Industry observers note that furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    Sources indicate that "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

    In a recent development, mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    It has been revealed that ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the firm to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

    Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent declared an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    It has been revealed that heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from new shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," mentioned Richardson.

    It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

    The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable company, regardless of market conditions.

    Richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

    Better Recent IPO: SpaceX or Anthropic?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:15PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
    • This has been an active year for IPOs.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    This has been an active year for IPOs. The two largest have been Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) and Anthropic (ANT -8.50%), which are among the leaders in their respective industries. Both companies sport eye-popping valuations, but considering the massive opportunities they have identified for their businesses, they might deliver outstanding returns even from current levels for investors willing to stay the course, if they can execute. But which one is the better buy today? Let's find out whether investors should invest in SpaceX or Anthropic right now.

    SpaceX's third-quarter revenue increased by 161% year over year to $14.6 billion. It reported a net profit of $4.4 billion, versus a net loss of $1.1 billion in the prior-year quarter. Those are strong results, largely attributable to SpaceX's Super Intelligence (SI) and connectivity segments, both of which were profitable in the quarter. SI revenue of $7.6 billion accounted for 52% of the manufacturer's top line.

    Recent findings suggest that spaceX's space launch segment is still operating at a loss, but the firm's opportunities in SI and connectivity are much larger. SpaceX identified a $28.5 trillion total addressable market, $26.5 trillion of which is within the artificial intelligence (AI) industry. The company is investing heavily to tap into this market. SpaceX is actively looking to increase its compute capacity to meet the soaring demand for AI compute.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that within a few years, the rocket firm might generate an even larger share of its revenue from its SI business, given how rapidly it is growing. In the meantime, the company's next-gen rocket, Starship, could unlock even more opportunities, including in AI and connectivity.

    Recent findings suggest that starship is still being tested, but it may help significantly reduce launch costs, thereby cutting operating expenses in the tech giant's space segment and enabling it to launch more satellites into orbit, including its newer, better Starlink V3 satellites and potentially AI satellites. We aren't there yet, but SpaceX's ambitions look promising. If the company can realize them, its stock could soar over the long run.

    Anthropic is now the record holder for the largest IPO ever, and the tech giant's recent financial results help explain why. In the third quarter, Anthropic's revenue grew 1,127% year over year to $17 billion. The company ended the period with a $71 billion annualized revenue run rate, and by the end of October, that had already grown to $81 billion.

    That highlights just how strong the demand for Anthropic's AI-powered tools is. Meanwhile, in the third quarter, the tech giant recorded an operating loss of $567 million, much better than the $3.1 billion loss in the third quarter of 2025. Regarding the bottom line, there is good news in bad news. Let's start with the latter.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Anthropic's Q3 net loss was a massive $23.3 billion, versus the net loss of $12.1 billion in the third quarter of 2025. But here's the good news: Most of that loss was due to non-cash charges resulting from increases in the fair value of various financial instruments. For long-term investors, that probably isn't the worst thing in the world, especially looking at Anthropic's pace of growth and the opportunities ahead.

    It has been revealed that the company wants to tap into the $40 trillion in economic value that knowledge workers create. Anthropic's AI tools help make these workers far more efficient and could unlock opportunities that were previously unattainable. And it has only begun to scratch the surface of the opportunities available to it. If all goes well, the stock may produce life-changing returns over the long run.

    According to recent reports, anthropic is generating higher revenue and growing faster than SpaceX, and it is also less expensive, at least based on both companies' price-to-sales (P/S) ratios. Based on Anthropic's $1.76 trillion market cap (on a fully diluted basis as of this writing) and its trailing 12-month revenue as of Sept. 30, the stock trades at 49.9x sales.

    It has been revealed that spaceX's P/S is 57.2. However, while SpaceX was profitable in the third quarter, Anthropic wasn't. Both remain unprofitable over the trailing 12-month period, but SpaceX will likely be in the green on the bottom line next year. What about both companies' opportunities? Their projected addressable markets may be a bit overstated, but there is no question that huge opportunities lie ahead for both.

    Recent findings suggest that so, which one is the better buy today? I'd pick SpaceX. It is closer to profitability, is the undisputed leader in space launch and satellite-based connectivity, and is more diversified than Anthropic. That stated, both stocks look like high-risk, high-reward plays. At current levels, only investors comfortable with significant volatility should consider either.

    #62321. Breaking: MSCI Is Cutting Strategy and Metaplanet From Its Indexes. Here's What It Means for Bitcoin Treasury Manufacturer Stocks.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (883 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: MSCI Is Cutting Strategy and Metaplanet From Its Indexes. Here's What It Means for Bitcoin Treasury Manufacturer Stocks.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • MSCI (MSCI -2.22%) made it official on Nov.
    • It has been revealed that the decision caps a fight that has run for more than a year.
    • I went back to Strategy's formal response, and wow.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Anders Bylund – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:17PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Strategy ›.

    MSCI (MSCI -2.22%) made it official on Nov. 11. Strategy (MSTR -9.67%), the software company turned Bitcoin (BTC +2.43%) treasury, will be deleted from the MSCI USA Index at the close of Nov. 30. Japan-based Bitcoin treasury peer Metaplanet (MTPLF -10.78%) is also on its way out, and Ethereum (ETH +4.36%) treasury company SharpLink (SBET -9.13%) lands on a latest public watch list.

    It has been revealed that the decision caps a fight that has run for more than a year. In October 2025, the market index manager proposed excluding any organization whose digital-asset holdings made up 50% or more of total assets. More than 250 organizations objected, and MSCI dropped the idea in January. In August, it came back with a broader screen aimed at "non-operating companies," built on five financial-ratio flags. Trip four of them, and you're out.

    I went back to Strategy's formal response, and wow. The letter calls the proposal "pretextual," suggesting that MSCI may be inventing reasons to exclude Strategy. The letter points out that this company alone makes up about 87% of the market value affected across all six names on the list of exclusions. Strategy insists that its Bitcoin business is an operating segment of an established software company, a treatment it states followed discussions with SEC staff.

    Fair points, some of them. When a supposedly neutral rule lands that heavily on one name, it's tough to call it a coincidence. It's like announcing a latest dress code that happens to ban exactly one guest's unusual hat.

    Recent findings suggest that then again, the same 10-page letter claims the exclusion would have "no meaningful impact" on Strategy's business. If it really doesn't matter, that's a lot of footnotes for a shrug.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that strategy held a special investor call on Nov. 19, eight days after the announcement. Executive Chairman Michael Saylor and CEO Phong Le spent the hour on preferred stock, credit markets, and Bitcoin-per-share metrics. The index removal never came up.

    Industry observers note that instead, the focus was the Strategy Stretch (STRC -1.01%) preferred stock. Le said Strategy has bought back about $3 billion of Stretch at $95 to $99 per share, after selling it on the open market at $100 per share. Saylor estimated that organic demand for the 12% instrument has shrunk from about $10.5 billion six months ago to roughly $7 billion today. The buybacks are meant to find that floor.

    According to recent reports, but no analysts asked questions on that call, and management never uttered the word "MSCI" on this seemingly convenient stage. The silence spoke volumes.

    Strategy's homepage is now essentially a Bitcoin cockpit, full of data on MSTR stock and the manufacturer's Bitcoin holdings. That's a strange look for a company that still sells analytics software, but the numbers are useful:.

    It has been revealed that that last one is the real gut punch. The market values Strategy at about 63% of its Bitcoin holdings. Even after subtracting $19.4 billion of debt and preferred stock, the stock trades at a slight discount to what's left.

    Sources indicate that the premium shimmer that let Strategy print stock and buy coins hand over fist has faded. Saylor himself indicates the stock-for-Bitcoin trade needs roughly a 1.29x multiple to make sense. There's a canyon between the existing mNAV and the required one.

    Index funds tracking MSCI benchmarks will have to sell their Strategy and Metaplanet shares by the end of November. Some of that selling was likely priced in after the August proposal, but forced selling is never handled with velvet gloves.

    The bigger matter is precedent. Other index providers, such as the S&P Dow Jones Indices group, have not adopted MSCI's screen. Strategy could still qualify for the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) index someday (if it meets many other requirements). But now there's a template that the others could follow. Any manufacturer that builds its balance sheet around a single digital asset has to consider that the passive-investing bid may not be a given.

    Metaplanet goes out the door with Strategy on Nov. 30, and SharpLink is standing in the hallway. The copycats that built their businesses on Saylor's playbook are learning that the operating plan didn't come with an index guarantee.

    Recent findings suggest that strategy isn't in trouble tomorrow. It has $4.7 billion in U.S. dollar reserves, which covers about 3.4 years of interest and dividends. That's a meaningful cash cushion.

    It has been revealed that but a cushion isn't a catalyst. Without the index bid, and trading at a discount to its own Bitcoin reserves, the old flywheel has stalled. The interesting question isn't whether Strategy survives. It's what it takes to bring back the lost mNAV premium.

    Airbnb vs. DoorDash: Which Stock Is a Better Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (803 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:25PM EST.
    • Investors often weigh growth potential against current profitability when comparing Airbnb (ABNB -1.41%) and DoorDash (DASH -2.88%).
    • Industry observers note that airbnb focuses on the global travel market by connecting hosts with guests seeking unique accommodations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:25PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Airbnb ›.

    Investors often weigh growth potential against current profitability when comparing Airbnb (ABNB -1.41%) and DoorDash (DASH -2.88%). Both companies have transformed how consumers spend on experiences and daily conveniences, but their financial trajectories remain distinct.

    Industry observers note that airbnb focuses on the global travel market by connecting hosts with guests seeking unique accommodations. DoorDash operates a local commerce platform that facilitates delivery from restaurants and retail merchants. While both benefit from digital shifts, their cost structures and capital requirements differ significantly.

    Recent findings suggest that airbnb operates a two-sided global marketplace that connects more than 5 million hosts with guests across roughly 220 countries. The manufacturer focuses on expanding its brand through strategic partnerships with cultural and entertainment organizations to attract a diverse range of travelers. This positioning within consumer discretionary stocks allows it to capture spending on both short-term vacations and long-term stays.

    According to recent reports, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $13.9 billion, representing growth of approximately 16.7% over the prior year. The firm demonstrated significant bottom-line strength by generating a net income of close to $3.2 billion during this same period. This level of profitability is a hallmark of its asset-light business model, which avoids the costs of owning physical properties.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    DoorDash operates a local commerce platform that connects merchants, consumers, and delivery couriers across more than 40 countries. The company has evolved beyond restaurant delivery into grocery and convenience sectors, maintaining agreements with over 600,000 merchants. Growth is further supported by over 56 million monthly active users and a proposed $17 billion acquisition of Instacart to solidify its market position.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $17.1 billion, which is a significant 35% increase compared to the previous twelve-month period. The company also reached a milestone by reporting a net income of approximately $1.1 billion.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Airbnb faces intense competition from established online travel agencies like Booking Holdings (BKNG -1.64%) and Expedia Group (EXPE -1.77%), as well as traditional hotel chains. The organization is also subject to evolving legal and regulatory environments, particularly restrictive short-term rental laws in major markets like Upcoming York City. Additionally, reliance on third-party payment processors and other threats present ongoing operational risks.

    Industry observers note that doorDash contends with fierce competition from other delivery platforms and merchants who develop their own direct-to-consumer ordering systems. The business model faces regulatory scrutiny regarding the classification of couriers as independent contractors, which could significantly impact labor costs. Furthermore, the company relies on third-party service providers like Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) Web Services for its platform stability and faces integration risks from its large-scale acquisition of Instacart.

    Airbnb appears more attractive based on future earnings estimates, while DoorDash carries a lower valuation when compared to its sales.

    DoorDash has a strong presence in the delivery space, but between DoorDash and Airbnb, I'd lean more toward Airbnb as an investable opportunity.

    One reason is that Airbnb is simply more profitable. While DoorDash's net income in the third quarter of 2026 climbed 91% to $466 million, it still pales in comparison to Airbnb's net income in the same quarter, at $1.9 billion. The other reason is that Airbnb's opportunities for expansion and revenue growth look more appealing. While DoorDash is acquiring Instacart, its platform is still more about restaurants, groceries, and broad delivery services. In comparison, Airbnb has more opportunities for expansion and integration that can lead to meaningful revenue growth by bundling car rentals, travel planning, and experiences into its offerings.

    Recent findings suggest that to get an idea of what to expect from Airbnb stock over the near term, analysts generally have a favorable outlook. According to CNN-tracked data, of the 46 analysts who cover the stock, 57% rate it a buy, 41% a hold, and 2% a sell. Of those analysts, the median one-year stock price forecast is $211, representing a gain of 23.8% from the price as of this writing, $170.36. The group's highest target is $245, representing a 43.8% gain, while the lowest target, $161, would be a 5.4% loss. While stock price forecasts aren't guarantees, the lowest projection indicates a 5% loss, so the risk-to-reward framework looks favorable.
